tips.title: Removing Old Paint from Kits
tips.text: To remove old paint from kit parts without damaging details, use a combination of alcohol and soap. Fill a small jar with warm water, add a few drops of dish soap and isopropyl alcohol. Place parts in the jar, swirl gently, then let soak for 15-30 minutes. Scrub with a soft toothbrush if needed, rinse with water, and dry. For tougher paint, use Mr. Hobby Mr. Color Thinner first, then alcohol-soap bath.

tips.title: Fixing Broken Photo-Etch Parts
tips.text: To repair broken photo-etch parts, use CA (Cyanoacrylate) glue like Testors Clear Sil-Gel. Apply a small amount onto the broken edge using a needle or brush, press parts together quickly and hold for 30 seconds. For better alignment, use tweezers and a small clamp. Once cured, paint over the repair with a matching color to hide it.

tips.title: Recovering Clogged Airbrushes
tips.text: To unclog a plugged airbrush nozzle, first soak it in Vallejo Airbrush Cleaner for 15 minutes. Then, gently push a needle (like a #18) through the nozzle to clear any dried paint. If still clogged, disassemble the airbrush, soak parts in acetone for 30 minutes, then scrub with a toothbrush and rinse with water. Reassemble and test.

tips.title: Repairing Warped Parts
tips.text: To fix warped plastic parts, place them between two pieces of glass or a flat surface. Lightly dampen a cloth with boiling water, wring it out, and place it on the warped side. Apply gentle pressure with the glass/cloth, allow cooling, then remove. For severe warping, use a hairdryer on low heat to gradually heat the warped area while applying gentle pressure.

tips.title: Avoiding Frost from Rattle Cans
tips.text: To prevent frost from forming on models when using rattle cans, apply a thin, even coat of Mr. Hobby Mr. Leveling Thinner first, allow it to flash off for 2-3 minutes, then apply the paint. This creates a smooth, even surface for the paint to adhere to, reducing the risk of frost. Avoid painting in cold or humid conditions.
